pulls.title: fix CDDL label collision + add grc.basis for result strength
pulls.author: nikolaichuk7
pulls.body:
Two changes, both against the CDDL in Section 4:

1. `grc.room-number` and `grc.hallway-number` both encoded to label 10 — a CBOR decode collision. Moved `room-number` to 13.

2. Adds an optional `grc.basis` (label 14), addressing #2. Rather than a closed list of positioning techniques (which would need extending every time a new one shows up), it reuses the three roles RFC 9334 already defines and this draft already cites normatively: `evidence` (the Attester itself produced the location — a signed GNSS fix, or the proximity measurement in Appendix A), `endorsement` (a third party vouches for it — e.g. a cloud provider's signed statement about a rack), `attestation-result` (a Verifier computed or inferred it — e.g. an operator-selected console region label, which today carries none of the strength of the first two but is indistinguishable from them in the current claims map). An optional `ref` points a Relying Party at the specific supporting claim by digest without embedding it, mirroring how draft-ietf-rats-endorsements keeps Endorsements separate from the Evidence they support.

Verified against a clean build: baseline idnits was 4 errors / 1 flaw / 3 warnings (all pre-existing, unrelated to this section); after this change, identical counts, nothing new introduced. The `&(...)` group-to-choice syntax follows RFC 8610 §2.2.2.2 verbatim.

Happy to adjust the label numbers or field names if you'd rather go a different direction — this is meant to open the specific design question in #2, not settle it.

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body:
The CDDL on this branch does not parse. With `eat.JC<J,C>` stubbed, using the `cddl` gem 0.12.14:

```
$ cat t.cddl
eat.JC<J, C> = C
grc.claim-uuid = eat.JC("corim.uuid-type", 12>

$ cddl t.cddl generate
*** Look for syntax problems around the %%% markers:
grc.claim-uuid = eat.JC%%%("corim.uuid-type", 12>
*** Parse error at 40 upto 40 of 64 (1410).
```

Lines 229 and 230 open the generic argument list with `(` and close it with `>`. Changing `(` to `<` on both fixes it — the `>` is already right. Control: `eat.JC<"corim.uuid-type", 12>` parses and emits `12`.

Fixing the delimiter surfaces two more inside the same five added lines:

```
Duplicate rule definition grm.provence
  -- old: >eat.JC<"grc.provence-values", 13>"]<  (line 230)
  -- new: >tstr .size 8"]<                       (line 233)

Unknown type grc.provence-values
  referenced at line 198, never defined
```

Separately, on the value type. `tstr .size 8` is exactly 8 bytes, so it rejects every form the Provenance Values section mandates:

```
x = tstr .size 8
  "RFC9711"        -> REJECT   (7)
  "RFC123456"      -> REJECT   (9)
  "I-D.something"  -> REJECT   (13)
```

`tstr / uint` accepts all three, and also the bare integer form the section describes.

Rebase note: the base here is `6c12383`, so this branch still carries `grc.hallway-number` and `grc.room-number` both at label 10. On current main `room-number` is 12, and 13 upward are free.

One naming thing, lowest priority: the CDDL spells `provence` while the section heading and registry name spell `Provenance`. The prose is already right.
